uncertain.text: c. cum lo- / cum, de ſponſ.
uncertain.note: note key 'k' has no {k} marker anywhere in the body. Every line of the annotation paragraph was checked at 4x–8x on the strips and on raw/img060.jpg; the only markers printed are {i} (line 3, after 'proces') and {l} (line 8, after 'religieuſes.'). The note stands beside 'ce. comme iadis…', so the omitted marker most likely belonged near 'ni violen-ce.' Compositor omission, not a reading doubt.

the cluster after 'c. penul' is hard: I read t + round s + i + hyphen ('penultsi-', continued 'me' = penultsime). Alternatives the reconciler should weigh: 'penulti-' (penultime), 'penultie-' (penultieme), 'penulisi-'. Checked at 900–1400% on raw/img060.jpg; the letter before the hyphen carries a dot (i) and the one before it is a round s.

the line-end hyphen after 'tranſ' is only partly inked — a faint broken stroke at x-height, much lighter than the solid hyphens of 'lite-' and 'lo-'. Read as a hyphen; could be an ink speck with the hyphen simply absent (which the conventions allow without comment).
third letter of 'ſpel.' is ink-filled; it shows a crossbar so I read 'e', but the expected abbreviation is 'ſpol.' (de restitutione spoliatorum). Could be 'ſpol.'

uncertain.text: terẽt le mariage: des robes, & veſtemens,
uncertain.note: the mark over the second 'e' of 'terẽt' is a thick wavy horizontal stroke (tilde), not the thin slanted acute the same page uses in 'ſterité' and 'tré'. Read as ẽ = 'terent'; a reader could take it for 'terét'.

sic: the '&' at the end of the previous line is repeated at the start of this one ('que deuant &' / '& apres.'). Transcribed as printed. The mark after 'apres' is a round dot on the baseline (period, not comma).
